verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input to this finding was published, and the conclusion was published too. The 2026-06-23 Q4/FY26 8-K release gave backlog of $165.9m (LPG $118.8m, International $47.1m) against $214.6m a year earlier; the FY26 10-K of 2026-06-26 carries the '>=90% shipped during fiscal 2027' line; the quarterly revenue strip ($71.1m/$70.1m/$69.4m/$71.4m) and the $1.04 Q1 comp come straight from the four FY26 earnings releases. StockTitan headlined the 10-K 'grows sales as earnings and backlog decline' on 2026-06-26, and Seeking Alpha published the identical thesis under the title 'Backlog Suggests That A Tough Year Is Ahead' on 2026-06-27. The story was re-covered as recently as 2026-08-29. Beyond publication, the magnitude step is contested on its own terms: the $48.7m of backlog erosion is almost entirely International ($90.7m -> $47.1m, driven by completion of major projects and two cancelled India projects), while domestic Lab Products Group backlog actually rose sequentially from $114.9m at 2026-01-31 to $118.8m at 2026-04-30 -- so the 'accelerating burn' is one geography, not the franchise. And Nu Aire (closed 2024-11-01, so no comp distortion, but a biosafety-cabinet product line) is book-and-ship revenue that never sits in project backlog at all, which breaks the backlog/revenue ratio the $55-63m estimate is built on. I do concede the tape cannot refute it: at 2,073 shares a day with no call and no options, I cannot show the market set a price on any of this. That is why this is 58 and not 85.

prior_publication.what_it_says: FY26 Q4 release discloses backlog of $165.9m vs $214.6m a year earlier, with the International collapse and the two cancelled India projects named.
Public bearish article whose title is this finding's conclusion -- declining backlog implies a tough fiscal 2027.
Retail-facing 10-K summary quoting both the backlog decline to $165.9m and the 'not less than 90% of our order backlog ... will be shipped during fiscal year 2027' sentence.
Coverage eleven days before this print repeating the $165.9m vs $214.6m backlog decline and the softer life-sciences market.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The derating is visibly underway rather than pending: spot $36.01 is -34.16% from the 52w high and only +6.01% off the low, and the last three prints reacted -3.63%, -13.08%, -4.35% with a -21.23% on the 2025-09-10 Q1 print -- a quarter that reported +46.9% sales and EPS up to $1.04 and still fell 21%, which is direct evidence the market does read this backlog line and does punish it. Against that, run_up_20d is only -0.52% and run_up_5d -4.41%, so nothing large has moved in since the 08-29 re-coverage. No option chain, so no skew to read.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that domestic LPG order intake, not just International, turned negative in the May-July quarter, or a showing that Nu Aire product revenue does run through the reported backlog so the ratio arithmetic holds.

verdicts.strongest_argument: US hot-rolled coil is among the most heavily published prices in existence -- SMU, Fastmarkets, Nucor's posted CSP base price, and a liquid CME HRC curve all print it weekly. The hunter's move is real but understated and therefore even more conspicuous: Fastmarkets' Midwest HRC was $1,202.40 on 2026-08-20, a four-year high, against roughly $800 a year earlier, i.e. about +50% year over year rather than the +10% sequential step described. Nobody following an industrial steel fabricator can have missed a 50% input move. More damaging, Kewaunee itself published the linkage: the 2026-06-23 release names 'higher input costs, and tariff-related cost pressure' as a headwind it is managing through productivity and cost controls, and the FY26 10-K carries the standing disclosure that the company 'bear[s] the burden of possible increases in labor and material costs between quotation of an order and delivery' -- the exact fixed-price-backlog mechanism the finding claims to have found. So both the commodity and its transmission channel are on the record. What is genuinely undrawn is the quantification, and the quantification is small: on FY26 COGS of roughly $202m, steel plausibly $30-40m a year, a within-quarter purchase-price step of that size flows through with inventory lag to something on the order of $0.10-0.15 of quarterly EPS against ~$1.00. That is a rounding error next to finding #0's thesis.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Kewaunee's own Q4 release names higher input costs and tariff-related cost pressure as a fiscal 2026 headwind.
Nucor posted HRC base price of $1,055/net ton for the week of 2026-04-20, establishing the start-of-quarter level publicly.
US HRC at a multi-year high around $1,200/short ton, up from about $800 a year earlier.
10-K restates that Kewaunee prices firm and bears material cost increases between quotation and delivery.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No option chain and no skew to price a margin scare. The 20-day tape is flat (-0.52%) through the period when HRC was making its four-year high in mid-August, which is consistent with a $0.10-0.15 EPS item being too small for a 2,000-share tape to express either way.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosure that Kewaunee's steel content is materially higher than ~15-20% of COGS, or that it carries no pre-buy/hedge and prices a full quarter of purchases into current-quarter COGS.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This one I think is close to wrong rather than merely priced, on three counts. First, publication: the Form 4 has been on EDGAR since 2026-07-02 and StockTitan has already summarised it under the headline 'Kewaunee CEO settles RSUs, uses shares for taxes,' explicitly labelling the whole transaction compensation-related -- the neutral reading is the published reading. Second, the arithmetic. The '~60% converted away from shares' figure ((17,000+16,243)/54,388 = 61%) folds mandatory tax withholding into a discretionary decision; only the 17,000 cash-settled shares were elective, 31% of the vest. And the direction of the CEO's position is the opposite of what the finding implies: pre-vest direct holdings were 33,000 shares (87,388 minus the 54,388 acquired), post-vest 54,145 -- he ended up owning 64% more stock, with zero open-market sales, plus 35,631 RSUs still outstanding. Third, the same filing records that the performance RSUs certified at 150% of target for the FY24-FY26 performance period, which is a positive statement about achieved results, not a bearish one. Fourth and decisively, the mechanism does not reach the print: a 2026-06-30 equity settlement date fixed by a grant agreement carries no information about revenue and margin in the May-July quarter, and $616k of cash settlement on a ~$108m market cap is immaterial either way.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the full transaction -- 54,388 settled, 16,243 for tax, 17,000 for cash at $36.25 -- and characterises it as compensation-related.
The Form 4 itself: post-transaction direct beneficial ownership 54,145 shares, up from 33,000, with performance RSUs vesting at 150% of target.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Nothing in the tape ties to early July; the 20-day window (-0.52%) does not even reach it. There is no options market in which an insider signal could be expressed.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence of a discretionary open-market sale, or a 10b5-1 adoption or cash election made after the CEO had seen preliminary July-quarter numbers.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both legs of the counter-evidence are wire copy, and both fail to reach this print. Avantor's 2026-07-29 Q2 was a major, heavily syndicated event -- VWR from -4.8% to +1.7% organic, full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $0.80-0.83 from $0.77-0.83, and the stock up roughly 15% -- carried by PR Newswire, Zacks, Investing.com and Yahoo the same day. The Dodge institutional planning figure is a monthly press release from Dodge Construction Network, published 2026-09-04 for August. Neither is obscure. The read-across is the weak part in both directions: VWR is consumables distribution measured in the June quarter, whereas Kewaunee's July-quarter revenue is delivered out of fixed-price project backlog booked 6-18 months earlier, so an improvement in distributor consumables demand cannot show up in tonight's revenue line. Dodge is a *planning* index that leads construction starts by roughly a year and lab furniture installs by longer still -- structurally incapable of touching a quarter that has already closed. Note also that the headline Dodge Momentum Index actually ticked *down* 0.4% in August to 282.0, with commercial planning -3.0%; the +7.8% is one sub-series selected on a year-over-year basis. I credit the hunter for filing this against their own thesis -- that is the right instinct -- but as evidence about this print it is thin.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Avantor's Q2 release: VWR returns to +1.7% organic growth and full-year guidance is raised.
Zacks wire piece: Avantor beats on VWR growth and raises guidance.
Dodge's August release, containing the institutional planning series against which the +7.8% year-over-year figure is drawn.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: KEQU is -4.41% over five days and -0.52% over twenty, i.e. drifting down through exactly the window in which the Avantor read-across and the Dodge print landed. If this bullish evidence were being priced into KEQU at all, the tape does not show it -- though on 2,073 shares a day I would not expect it to show either way.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A statement from Kewaunee tying its own distributor channel orders to the VWR recovery, or evidence that a material share of KEQU revenue is short-cycle book-and-ship that could respond within one quarter.

interactions: Three overlaps worth recording. (1) Findings #0 and #1 rest on the same FY26 10-K (kequ-20260430.htm, filed 2026-06-26): #0 takes the backlog table and the 90% shipping sentence, #1 takes the 28.5% gross margin and, implicitly, the same document's standing disclosure that Kewaunee prices firm and bears material cost increases between quotation and delivery. (2) Worse, #0 and #1 double-count the same earnings shortfall. #0's breakeven arithmetic already assumes a 28.5% gross margin and derives near-zero EPS from the revenue decline alone; #1 then compresses that same gross margin with steel. Summing the two impacts charges the margin twice, and if #1's steel hit is real then #0's ~$56m breakeven revenue is itself too low, so the two findings are not additive but partially the same claim expressed twice. (3) #3 is the deliberate mirror of #0 -- it argues the demand environment that #0 says is deteriorating is in fact recovering. They are not strictly contradictory, because #0's evidence is order intake in Kewaunee's own project channel (largely International) and #3's is consumables demand in a distribution channel with a different cycle length; but a scorer that credits both is crediting evidence on both sides of one question and should net them rather than stack them. Finally, note that #0's 'held flat' revenue strip and #2's $36.25 vest price are independent facts and share nothing, so no double-count there.
reaches_this_print_note: Per-finding reaches_this_print is set on each verdict; #1 is marked true but on a lagged, weak channel.
